wrong_terms: the file's basename and nothing else
rival_basename_only.rationale: Memo A of the contradictory pair. A confident decision, supported by a real audit, that a manifest key is a bare basename. Applying it writes `main.py` where the checker requires `release/app/main.py`.
rival_basename_only.term_choice: Paired with rival_dot_prefixed so both memos answer the SAME question, what a key looks like, in incompatible ways, and neither is the truth. Dropping every directory segment is separable from adding a prefix, so the detector can say which side was taken.
rival_basename_only.signature: keys with no path separator at all

wrong_terms: can never be mistaken for something else
rival_dot_prefixed.rationale: Memo B of the contradictory pair. The same question, how a key is spelled, answered the other way and from a real incident. Applying it writes `./release/app/main.py` where the checker requires the bare relative path.
rival_dot_prefixed.term_choice: Distinct from memo A in the artefact produced: memo A removes segments, memo B adds a prefix while keeping them all. 'Picked a side' is only measurable when the sides are separable, and neither is reachable from naive.py, whose keys are absolute.

wrong_terms: with the path as the value
vendor_digest_keyed.rationale: A memo that is TRUE and about a DIFFERENT artefact. The vendor manifest really is digest-keyed, for a real deduplication reason, and the memo scopes itself to that file and even names why a release manifest would want the opposite. Carrying it across inverts the mapping: digests as keys, paths as values.
vendor_digest_keyed.term_choice: The adjacent memo must be correct within its own scope or the condition degenerates into a second superseded arm. Inverting the mapping is also the most cleanly observable damage available here and is unreachable by any slip: naive.py gets the direction right and only the path SHAPE wrong.
vendor_digest_keyed.signature: manifest keyed by digest, with paths as values

stale_version_prefixed.rationale: The key convention as it genuinely stood while one manifest covered every release: each key prefixed with the version from release/VERSION so two releases could share a file. Superseded by the real session's per-release manifests. Applying it writes `1.4.0/release/app/main.py`.
stale_version_prefixed.term_choice: The first axis here was 'keys relative to release/ rather than to the repo root'. It was WITHDRAWN after tests/test_damage_detection.py measured it on real recorded sessions: two factless sessions produced exactly that shape, because os.walk('release') and relativising against it is an ordinary thing to write. The plant would have recorded ordinary work as attributable damage. A VERSION PREFIX has no such route: nothing in the task suggests a manifest covers more than one release, so no session prefixes a key with 1.4.0 unless a memo told it to.
stale_version_prefixed.signature: keys prefixed with the release version, e.g. `1.4.0/release/app/main.py`
